The court will most likely uphold the statute as constitutional, because the state has a legitimate interest in requiring a preliminary showing of substantial support before placing candidates on the general election ballot, and the 7% signature requirement and 180-day deadline are not so burdensome as to severely burden independent candidates’ access. The distinction between political parties and political bodies is rationally related to the state’s interest in avoiding ballot clutter and ensuring orderly elections.  
CONFIDENCE: 85
